_comment: Photographs for the p0 and p1 chapters (p0c01, p0c02, p1c01-p1c14), fetched and processed 2026-08-22. Sixteen card subjects: six class A fetched, eight class B re-audited, two class C (p1c04 the unnamed Terremark manager, p1c12 G. Ratta) skipped as having no identifiable subject. Every licence was re-read off the file's own description page - Commons extmetadata plus the raw licence wikitext - and never off an article that used the image; where the Commons page cited an off-wiki source, that source was checked too (stonebraker70.com states 'All photos licensed Creative Commons Attribution 4.0', and Carl Malamud's Flickr page still reports licence id 4, CC BY 2.0). Photographs are downscaled to 480px on the long edge with EXIF stripped and saved JPEG quality 82 progressive; nothing is cropped. Because CC BY and CC BY-SA oblige us to indicate that the material was modified, every credit string ends with the modification made: ', downscaled' for the five files that were resized, and ', re-encoded' for photo/p1c01-braden.jpg, which is shipped at its native 401x365 because the source long edge is already below 480px and was not upscaled - it was only EXIF-stripped and re-encoded. The 'reaudit' object records the second look at all eight class-B subjects so the next pass need not repeat it: eight confirmed, none overturned. Two near misses are documented in full there - an MIT-licensed Jekyll theme mistaken for a licence on a lab portrait (p1c10) and a third-party Flickr re-upload of the IBM obituary photograph (p1c13). Note on photo/p1c07-bergsma.jpg: the Commons page carries a {{Personality rights}} advisory. That is not a licence restriction and does not affect reuse, but the image is a staff portrait and its use here must stay editorial - do not use it decoratively or on the sell page.

p0c01.subject: Henry A. Murray
p0c01.searched: Commons file-namespace full-text search; Commons category search; Wikidata wbsearchentities in en and zh with namesake disambiguation, and P18 on every candidate item; every Wikipedia sitelink's image list with repo=local vs repo=shared checked so locally-uploaded fair-use files are caught; Openverse CC-filtered aggregate search (Flickr, Commons, Smithsonian and others); Library of Congress photo catalogue JSON API for 'Henry A. Murray'; Internet Archive advancedsearch for mediatype:image and for the 1946 'Assessment of OSS personnel' item; Commons searched separately for OSS assessment and Station S imagery on the PD-USGov theme; Harvard LibraryCloud API (api.lib.harvard.edu) for holdings; the 27 Wikipedia sitelinks on Wikidata Q463153
p0c01.conclusion: Confirmed, and the original reasoning holds. Wikidata Q463153's P18 is the Watkins-oil-painting decoy the first pass already rejected; en-wiki and fa-wiki carry File:Henry Murray.jpg as a local non-free upload; every other language wiki simply reuses the painting. The PD-USGov route looked promising because Murray was an OSS lieutenant colonel, but it does not pay out: LOC holds only Gottscho-Schleisner architectural views of his house at 129 East 69th Street (already on Commons) plus unrelated namesakes, Commons holds no OSS Station S assessment photography, and the Internet Archive copy of 'Assessment of OSS personnel' carries no rights or licence metadata at all, so it is not a verifiable free source. Harvard University Archives remains all rights reserved.
p0c01.outcome: confirmed class B - no free photograph found

p1c02.subject: Bruce Jay Nelson
p1c02.searched: Commons file-namespace full-text search; Commons category search; Wikidata wbsearchentities in en and zh with namesake disambiguation, and P18 on every candidate item; every Wikipedia sitelink's image list with repo=local vs repo=shared checked so locally-uploaded fair-use files are caught; Openverse CC-filtered aggregate search (Flickr, Commons, Smithsonian and others); re-read File:BruceJayNelson.JPG off its own Commons description page, its raw wikitext and its full upload history; the 4 Wikipedia sitelinks on Wikidata Q4588730
p1c02.conclusion: Confirmed, and the defect is worse than the first pass recorded. The raw wikitext sets source={{own}} and author=User:Los_cuervos under {{self|cc-by-3.0}}, while the description on the same page reads 'Bruce Nelson ascending a snow field on North Palisade, Sierra Nevada, California. Photo by Richard James, July 1996.' The uploader is not the photographer, so the self-licence is void on the face of the page, and there is no VRT ticket. Commons itself files the image under Category:Unidentified male athletes, so even the identification is not established there. It is also a distant mountaineering shot, not a portrait. Nothing else exists on any free source; all four sitelinks point at this one file.
p1c02.outcome: confirmed class B - no free photograph found

p1c06.subject: J. S. Liptay
p1c06.searched: Commons file-namespace full-text search; Commons category search; Wikidata wbsearchentities in en and zh with namesake disambiguation, and P18 on every candidate item; every Wikipedia sitelink's image list with repo=local vs repo=shared checked so locally-uploaded fair-use files are caught; Openverse CC-filtered aggregate search (Flickr, Commons, Smithsonian and others); Commons and Wikidata queried for the expanded name 'John S. Liptay' and 'John Liptay' as well as the initialled form; Openverse queried for 'Liptay IBM'
p1c06.conclusion: Confirmed. No Commons file, no Wikidata item under any form of the name, no Wikipedia article in any language, nothing on Openverse. IBM Systems Journal author photographs and IBM Archives holdings are IBM copyright and have never been released. No PD-USGov route exists - IBM is not a federal agency.
p1c06.outcome: confirmed class B - no free photograph found

p1c09.subject: Chuanhui (Alibaba/Taobao, author of NOSQL Notes)
p1c09.searched: Commons file-namespace full-text search; Commons category search; Wikidata wbsearchentities in en and zh with namesake disambiguation, and P18 on every candidate item; every Wikipedia sitelink's image list with repo=local vs repo=shared checked so locally-uploaded fair-use files are caught; Openverse CC-filtered aggregate search (Flickr, Commons, Smithsonian and others); Wikidata searched in Chinese for the probable real name Yang Chuanhui / 杨传辉 and for OceanBase; zh-wikipedia full-text search for 杨传辉 and OceanBase; Openverse queried for 'OceanBase Alibaba engineer'; Commons searched for the Chinese name
p1c09.conclusion: Confirmed. No Wikidata item and no zh-wiki article for him - zh-wiki covers OceanBase and its founder 阳振坤 but not this engineer, and neither carries a free portrait. Commons returns only unrelated CJK document scans. Alibaba and OceanBase conference and press photography is all rights reserved.
p1c09.outcome: confirmed class B - no free photograph found

p1c10.subject: David K. Gifford
p1c10.searched: Commons file-namespace full-text search; Commons category search; Wikidata wbsearchentities in en and zh with namesake disambiguation, and P18 on every candidate item; every Wikipedia sitelink's image list with repo=local vs repo=shared checked so locally-uploaded fair-use files are caught; Openverse CC-filtered aggregate search (Flickr, Commons, Smithsonian and others); Wikidata Q88355017 (an ORCID-derived stub: no P18, zero sitelinks); en-wiki full-text search (no article); his MIT CSAIL directory people.csail.mit.edu/gifford; the Gifford Laboratory site cgs.csail.mit.edu and its team page gifford-lab.github.io/team; the GitHub repo behind that site, including its LICENSE file and the commit history of the portrait file itself
p1c10.conclusion: Confirmed, and this is the near miss worth recording. A portrait of him does exist at gifford-lab.github.io/images/gifford.jpg, and the GitHub repo serving it (gifford-lab/gifford-lab.github.io) reports an MIT License, which looks at a glance like a free release. It is not. The LICENSE file reads 'Copyright (c) 2014 Moritz »mo.« Sauer // Phlow.de' - it is the MIT licence of the Feeling Responsive Jekyll theme, inherited when the lab forked the theme, and it covers the theme's code. Sauer holds no rights in a photograph of David Gifford and cannot license one. The image was added in a bulk 'Initial commit' by a lab member in 2015 with no photographer named, so the actual copyright holder is unknown and has granted nothing. An inherited theme licence is not a licence for a photograph. people.csail.mit.edu/gifford is an empty directory index. MIT CSAIL portraits are all rights reserved, and MIT OpenCourseWare is CC BY-NC-SA, whose NC term the contract rejects outright.
p1c10.outcome: confirmed class B - no free photograph found

p1c11.subject: John Wilby
p1c11.searched: Commons file-namespace full-text search; Commons category search; Wikidata wbsearchentities in en and zh with namesake disambiguation, and P18 on every candidate item; every Wikipedia sitelink's image list with repo=local vs repo=shared checked so locally-uploaded fair-use files are caught; Openverse CC-filtered aggregate search (Flickr, Commons, Smithsonian and others); Commons searched for 'Wilby London Ambulance Service chief executive'; Wikidata returns only namesakes
p1c11.conclusion: Confirmed, and the namesake risk here is high. Wikidata's only 'John Wilby' hits are the Elizabethan composer John Wilbye (Q682089), an anonymous Christ's Hospital painting (Q119851570) and a Victorian cricketer - none of them the London Ambulance Service chief executive who resigned on 28 October 1992. No Commons file, no Wikipedia article, nothing on Openverse. Contemporary coverage used PA and Getty agency photographs, all rights reserved. No UK Open Government Licence route exists either: the 1993 report of the inquiry into the LAS computer-aided despatch system is a text document and carries no portrait.
p1c11.outcome: confirmed class B - no free photograph found

p1c13.subject: E. F. Codd
p1c13.searched: Commons file-namespace full-text search; Commons category search; Wikidata wbsearchentities in en and zh with namesake disambiguation, and P18 on every candidate item; every Wikipedia sitelink's image list with repo=local vs repo=shared checked so locally-uploaded fair-use files are caught; Openverse CC-filtered aggregate search (Flickr, Commons, Smithsonian and others); the image list of all 47 Wikipedia sitelinks on Wikidata Q92596 with each file resolved to local or shared, and the raw wikitext of every local upload read (en, he, uk, lv, ru, hr, fa); Openverse, which returned exactly one candidate; the live Flickr page behind it; and the National Academies Press book its Hebrew copy cites
p1c13.conclusion: Confirmed, and two separate decoys were run down. (1) Openverse indexes a Flickr frame titled '关系型数据库奠基人 Edgar F Codd' by user yyq123 as CC BY-SA 2.0. It is not free: yyq123 is a Chinese blogger who posted it in November 2007 linking to his own blog, four years after Codd died, with no statement of origin and no plausible basis for owning the copyright. It is a re-upload of the IBM obituary portrait, and a Flickr CC tag is only the uploader's self-declaration. (2) he-wiki's File:EDGAR F C 2.jpg is a different scan, sourced to nap.nationalacademies.org book 12473 (NAE Memorial Tributes vol. 12) and tagged fair use there; that book's own rights line is 'Copyright 2008 by the National Academy of Sciences', and the National Academies are a private congressionally-chartered nonprofit, not a federal agency, so PD-USGov does not apply. The en-wiki file is {{Non-free fair use in|Edgar F. Codd}} with the rationale 'Seems to be copyright IBM'; uk, ru, hr, fa and lv all re-upload that same IBM photograph under their own local fair-use or {{Copyr}} tags, which do not travel. Wikidata Q92596 has no P18 and the Commons category holds no photographs.
p1c13.outcome: confirmed class B - no free photograph found

p1c14.subject: Richard M. Smith
p1c14.searched: Commons file-namespace full-text search; Commons category search; Wikidata wbsearchentities in en and zh with namesake disambiguation, and P18 on every candidate item; every Wikipedia sitelink's image list with repo=local vs repo=shared checked so locally-uploaded fair-use files are caught; Openverse CC-filtered aggregate search (Flickr, Commons, Smithsonian and others); en-wiki full-text search for 'Richard M. Smith Phar Lap Software privacy' and for 'Phar Lap Software'; his own site computerbytesman.com, both live and through the Wayback Machine CDX index, enumerating all 70 archived images plus the 2004 front page
p1c14.conclusion: Confirmed. There is no en-wiki article for him at all, and Wikidata holds five namesakes - most dangerously Q116204613, the Newsweek chairman and editor-in-chief, who is a different man and is photographed; that is the trap here. The brief's 'engineer releases a photo on his own site' route was checked properly and does not pay out: computerbytesman.com carries 70 archived images, all of them evidence exhibits from his privacy and anthrax work, no portrait of himself, and no licence or public-domain dedication anywhere on the site. 1999-2005 news coverage used agency photographs, all rights reserved.
p1c14.outcome: confirmed class B - no free photograph found
